1␟Daxing: Daxing was the brand-new capital city the Sui dynasty built southeast of old Chang'an in the 580s, laid out on a strict north-south grid. The later Tang dynasty inherited it and renamed it Chang'an.
1␟Yuwen Kai: Yuwen Kai was the master architect under the Sui dynasty who designed the new capital Daxing, planning its huge grid layout, and also engineered key stretches of the Grand Canal.
2␟Wordless Stele: The Wordless Stele is a tall blank stone monument standing at the tomb of China's only female emperor, Wu Zetian. Famously left without any inscription, it still stands today.
4␟Mawei Station: Mawei Station was a post stop about 60 miles west of the Tang capital Chang'an where, during a desperate flight from rebellion, the emperor's own guards mutinied and forced the death of his favorite consort.
6␟Slender Gold: Slender Gold was a distinctive calligraphy style invented by the Song emperor Huizong, with extremely thin, sharp strokes that look like twisted gold wire. It is still practiced and admired today.
9␟Lü Wenhuan: Lü Wenhuan was the Song dynasty commander who held the fortress city of Xiangyang against relentless Mongol siege for six years before it finally fell, opening the way for the Mongol conquest of southern China.
